Revised Roadmap: 3-4 Months to AI Developer 
This is a comprehensive, topic-by-topic checklist with a timeline for a high-intensity, 3-4 
month learning plan. 
Month 1: The Foundations 
●​ Week 1: Python & Basics (Days 1-7) 
○​ Python Syntax & Data Types (lists, dicts, tuples, sets). 
○​ Control Flow (if/else, loops) and Functions. 
○​ Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts. 
○​ Project: Simple calculator or number guessing game. 
●​ Week 2: NumPy, Pandas & Git (Days 8-14) 
○​ NumPy arrays, slicing, broadcasting, and vectorized operations. 
○​ Pandas DataFrames, data cleaning, filtering, and grouping. 
○​ Git/GitHub: Committing, pushing, and managing a code repository. 
○​ Project: Analyze and clean a simple dataset. 
●​ Week 3: Visualization & Foundational Math (Days 15-21) 
○​ Data Visualization with Matplotlib and Seaborn. 
○​ Linear Algebra: Vectors, matrices, and dot products. 
○​ Calculus: The concepts of derivatives and gradients. 
○​ Project: Create visualizations to tell a story from your dataset. 
●​ Week 4: Probability, Stats & Portfolio Building (Days 22-28) 
○​ Probability & Statistics: Descriptive stats (mean, median), Bayes' Theorem. 
○​ Finalize and document your foundational projects on GitHub. 
Month 2: Core ML & The Deep Learning Bridge 
●​ Week 5: Core ML & Model Evaluation (Days 29-35) 
○​ ML Fundamentals: Supervised vs. Unsupervised Learning, the ML workflow. 
○​ Algorithms: Linear/Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). 
○​ Metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, Confusion Matrix. 
○​ Project: Build a classifier on a classic dataset (e.g., Iris or Titanic). 
●​ Week 6: Unsupervised Learning & Deep Learning Intro (Days 36-42) 
○​ Unsupervised: K-Means clustering, Principal Component Analysis (PCA). 
○​ Deep Learning: The Neuron, activation functions, and the concept of 
forward/backward propagation. 
●​ Week 7: Transformers & Embeddings (Days 43-49) 
○​ The Transformer Architecture: Understand the intuition behind the attention 
mechanism. 
○​ Text Embeddings: Learn how to convert text into numerical vectors using 
pre-trained models from Hugging Face. 
○​ Project: Generate embeddings for a set of documents and perform a basic 
semantic search. 
●​ Week 8: LLMs & Prompt Engineering (Days 50-56) 
○​ LLM Concepts: What LLMs are and how they differ from traditional models. 
○​ API Usage: Learn to use APIs from OpenAI or Hugging Face.

○​ Prompt Engineering: The art of creating effective prompts. 
○​ Project: Build a simple chatbot using an LLM API. 
Month 3: RAG & Fine-Tuning 
●​ Week 9: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) (Days 57-63) 
○​ Vector Databases: The purpose and use of a vector database (e.g., 
ChromaDB, Pinecone). 
○​ The RAG Pipeline: The full process of document chunking, embedding, 
retrieval, and generation. 
○​ Project: Build a Q&A application over a custom PDF or set of documents 
using a library like LangChain or LlamaIndex. 
●​ Week 10: Fine-Tuning (Days 64-70) 
○​ Theory: The difference between fine-tuning and prompt engineering, and 
when to use each. 
○​ PEFT: Learn about Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) and techniques 
like LoRA. 
○​ Practice: Fine-tune a pre-trained model on a specific task using the Hugging 
Face ecosystem. 
Month 4: Specialization & Capstone Project 
●​ Week 11: Advanced Concepts & MLOps (Days 71-77) 
○​ Advanced RAG: Learn multi-query retrieval and other advanced techniques. 
○​ MLOps for LLMs: Containerization with Docker and serving a model with a 
framework like FastAPI. 
●​ Weeks 12-16: The Capstone Project (Days 78-120) 
○​ Problem Definition: Choose a problem to solve using RAG or fine-tuning 
that is more complex than your previous projects. 
○​ Full Implementation: Build the entire application from start to finish. 
○​ Documentation: Create a detailed README, explaining your project's 
architecture. 
○​ Deployment: Deploy a functional prototype to a cloud service to showcase 
your work.
